# Java TCK requirement-to-translation scaffold

Generated from `compliance/catalogs/java-tck-scenario-catalog.json`. This is an authoring index, not a conformance report.

## Scope and evidence rules

This scaffold indexes every stable `requirement_id` currently present in the portable Java scenario catalog, and every cataloged scenario sketch. The catalog's `api_methods`, `adapter_inputs`, `contract_refs`, `java_test`, and `parity` fields remain the detailed source for each sketch.

The index is not a claim that these IDs exhaust IEEE 1516.1-2025 normative requirements. An ID-to-scenario link is traceability, not proof of a test or a normative clause mapping. Only mappings explicitly recorded in `requirement_mappings` are shown as exact section links; do not infer clause numbers from titles, C++ IDs, or broad contract references.

`default_status` is harness configuration, not provider evidence: `run` means enabled by default and `unsupported` means not enabled pending adapter/provider support. Neither means the provider passed. A C++ `parity` value is a source-case pointer, not proof that the Java behavior is equivalent until the assertions and lifecycle are reviewed.

Portable Java sources remain limited to JDK types and `hla.rti1516_2025` API types. Provider selection, JARs, FOM/MIM, endpoint, and callback configuration belong at the adapter boundary. No implementation-specific assertion belongs in this TCK.

## Translation card to complete for each promoted case

Use the matching catalog scenario row as the starting card. Complete these before calling a translated case verified:

1. Record the C++ TCK scenario ID and exact source test symbol; inspect only the relevant source/test range and existing evidence. A pointer alone is not a behavior review.
2. Summarize the observable contract as preconditions, service calls, callback/event sequence, assertions, and cleanup. Keep assertions at the public Java API boundary.
3. Verify the exact IEEE 1516.1-2025 clause/subclause mapping from an authoritative requirement source. Add only a supported, direct mapping; label internal/API-only checks explicitly.
4. List the standard Java API methods and adapter inputs (provider JAR/factory, FOM/MIM, endpoint, callback model, logical-time configuration, and any test data). Do not add vendor flags or implementation classes.
5. Check equivalent callback servicing modes when the behavior is callback-sensitive, then record compile evidence separately from provider runtime results.
6. Keep scenarios unsupported until a provider run artifact demonstrates the behavior. Record provider, adapter profile, result, and failure detail in the normal evidence path.
7. If no direct portable behavior exists, record a reasoned not-applicable/API-contract-only disposition rather than inventing a test.

## Explicit non-normative/API-only dispositions

- `java-tck.callback-reentrancy` — No rationale recorded.
- `java-tck.receive-order-multi-attribute-update-callback-cancellation` — Provider, compatible multi-attribute FOM, endpoint, object/attribute names, and callback model are adapter-supplied. Remains unsupported by default until executed against an IEEE 1516.1-2025 Java provider.
- `java-tck.regional-three-dimensional-overlap` — Requires the adapter-supplied three-dimensional FOM via hla.rti.tck.threeDimensionalFom, configured object and attribute names, and three dimension names. Uses only the official Java API.
- `java-tck.service-report-interaction-dimensions-invalid-handle-contexts` — Opt-in because the companion needs a separate additional FOM execution. Configure hla.rti.tck.additionalFom with fom-extension-tck.xml alongside the primary dimensional FOM, standard MIM, logical-time implementation, provider, endpoint, and callback model. Runtime evidence is local Umbra JNI only.
- `java-tck.service-report-object-dimensions-invalid-handle-contexts` — Opt-in because the focused companion needs a separate additional FOM execution. Configure hla.rti.tck.additionalFom with fom-extension-tck.xml plus the primary dimensional FOM, standard MIM, logical-time implementation, provider, endpoint, and callback model. Runtime evidence is local Umbra JNI only.
- `java-tck.service-report-timestamped-object-deletion` — Default-disabled because execution requires adapter-supplied FOM, standard MIM, logical-time implementation, callback model, and installed Java provider. Current-source Umbra JNI execution passed both callback models on 2026-11-15; local-provider evidence does not establish independent-provider interoperability or conformance.
- `java-tck.logical-time-data-elements-contract` — No rationale recorded.
- `java-tck.attribute-value-request-service-boundaries-invalid-handle-contexts` — Opt-in Java TCK scenario: RtiTckMain registers defaultEnabled=false, so it is reported unsupported by the default suite unless selected through a capability profile or enabled with -Dhla.rti.tck.runUnverified=true.

## Explicit C++ source-case scope dispositions

These entries classify C++ source behaviors that do not belong in a portable Java TCK, or identify the limited standard slice that is covered separately. They are not provider results.

- `java-tck.cpp-variable-length-data-no-direct-equivalent` (`not applicable`) — **C++ VariableLengthData ownership and pointer-storage contract:** IEEE 1516.1-2025 Java exposes byte arrays and DataElement values rather than a VariableLengthData class or pointer-adoption API. Java Credentials also exposes its backing array, so C++ copy/assignment ownership semantics are not portable Java assertions.
- `cpp-tck.logical-time-data-elements-cpp-only-operations` (`not applicable`) — **C++ clone/copy, dynamic-type, and vector-offset assertions for logical-time DataElements:** The Java API exposes HLAlogicalTime and HLAlogicalTimeInterval DataElement wrappers, and java-tck.logical-time-data-elements-contract covers their Java-visible value, encoding, decoding, boundary, cursor, and malformed-input behavior. C++ clone/copy independence, dynamic-type compatibility overloads, and vector encodeInto/decodeFrom(offset) have no Java API counterpart and remain excluded.
- `java-tck.provider-implementation-boundary` (`not applicable`) — **Provider implementation classes and implementation-only state-machine tests:** The portable Java TCK may change only API/provider JARs, factory name, FOM/MIM inputs, and capability profile. Provider implementation evidence remains in the provider's own compliance lane.
- `java-tck.provider-internal-policy` (`not applicable`) — **Provider-internal transport, persistence, allocator, and authorization implementation details:** Only behavior observable through hla.rti1516_2025 is portable; implementation-specific evidence remains in the provider's own compliance lane.
- `cpp-tck.pending-negotiated-ownership-package-filesystem-restore-implementation-assertions` (`not applicable`) — **Per-join report-file allocation, filesystem identity/contents, and report append policy across restore:** The portable negotiated ownership and save/restore behavior is covered by java-tck.pending-negotiated-ownership-save-restore, and the standard public HLAreportServiceFile value is covered separately by java-tck.federate-mom-report-service-file. Exact paths, distinct files per join, file-set stability, filesystem contents, and append-gating are provider implementation details and are not portable HLA assertions.
- `cpp-tck.service-report-file-connect-failure` (`not applicable`) — **Connect failure caused by an unusable service-report directory, exception classification, and retry policy:** The candidate has no direct normative clause mapping. Filesystem failure injection, RTIinternalError classification, fallback policy, and retry after repair are provider-specific behaviors, not portable IEEE 1516.1-2025 TCK assertions.
- `cpp-tck.service-report-file-creation-failure` (`not applicable`) — **Join failure caused by service-report file creation, rollback/discovery policy, and retry behavior:** The candidate has no direct normative clause mapping. Filesystem failure injection, exception classification, failed-join rollback/discovery policy, and retry after repair are provider-specific behaviors, not portable IEEE 1516.1-2025 TCK assertions.

## Known limits and next handoff

- The requirement index covers catalog-linked IDs, not an independently enumerated set of every normative paragraph in IEEE 1516.1-2025. Building that full standard clause inventory and reconciling it to these scenarios is a separate traceability task.
- Exact clause mappings are sparse in the current catalog. Close those mapping gaps before claiming normative requirement coverage, even when a scenario already exists or compiles.
- Use the read-only parity audit to locate C++ catalog cases without a Java parity link: `python tools/audit_cpp_java_tck_parity.py --report-cpp-gaps`. Classify each gap for standard portability before translating it.
- This work is Java-catalog/documentation only; C++ sources are not rebuilt by the scaffold generator.
